1-2: Even and odd numbers: which number of a list is even.
Beads in a repeating pattern of two colours: the colour of a given bead.
Children in pairs: how many are left without a pair.
A lamp or a door switched again and again: on or off, open or shut, after a given number of turns.
Odd or even numbers in order, such as the house numbers on one side of a street: a given one, or how many up to a number.
A sum of a few odd numbers: even or odd, by how many numbers there are.
A circle of boys and girls standing in turn: how many of each.
A frog jumping two stones at a time: which stones it can land on.
Sweets shared equally between two friends and between some other number of friends.
Coins turned over one at a time: after how many turns they can all lie the other way up.
3-4: The sum of two numbers is odd: what the other number can be.
How many odd numbers there are in a range.
A repeating pattern, of beads on a string or a traffic light's colours: what comes at a far-off place.
A product of two numbers is odd: what that says about both of them.
A grasshopper jumping one step left or right each time: where it can be after some jumps.
A sum of many odd numbers, such as the cost of several things at an odd price: even or odd by how many there are.
The sum of the odd numbers against the sum of the even numbers in a range.
A circle of children: whether boys and girls can take turns all the way round.
Coins turned over two at a time: the fewest moves to show all heads.
Number cards split into two piles with equal sums: which sets can be split.
5-6: Steps that add or multiply: which numbers can be reached.
A knight on a chessboard: the colour of its square after some moves.
A sum of many numbers is odd: how many of them can be even.
Adding 1 to two numbers at a time: the fewest steps to make them all equal.
Dominoes on a board with two corners cut off: how many fit.
A walk on a grid of squares: whether it can end where it began after an odd number of steps.
Frogs jumping over one another on a line: which places are possible.
Switching three lamps in a row at a time: whether all of them can be on.
Bugs crawling to neighbouring squares: how many squares can be left empty.
Handshakes at a party: how many people shook an odd number of hands.
